The disclosure of information on October 9, 2026, brought Pfizer's long-suppressed list of adverse effects before the public eye.

Pharmaceutical companies and their allied media spent four years downplaying concerns; skeptics were branded as "conspiracy theorists" and "science deniers."

This update draws from Pfizer's own compilation of reported side effects—data that was withheld even as the public was assured harms were rare and mild.

The list goes far beyond fever or fatigue; it is a record of serious, deadly, and life-altering health conditions acknowledged by the company itself.

Blood clotting cases include clots that can lead to stroke, heart attack, or pulmonary embolism, plus deep vein thrombosis, hepatic and spinal artery thrombosis, innominate vein thrombosis, and ventricular mural thrombi. Brainstem embolism and thrombosis are also listed as blockages that can result in loss of motor function, breathing, and death.

Hundreds of cardiac arrest cases were recorded; terms like heart failure, cardiogenic shock, myocarditis, and pericarditis describe conditions where the heart becomes inflamed, weakened, or stops working. "Sudden death" is explicitly mentioned.

Neurological cases are no less severe; the list includes acute flaccid myelitis (paralysis resembling polio), hemorrhagic encephalitis and brainstem encephalitis, central nervous system vasculitis, frontal and temporal lobe epilepsy, generalized tonic-clonic seizures, neonatal seizures, epileptic psychosis, facial paralysis, and Hashimoto's encephalopathy. Conditions like acute kidney injury, autoimmune hepatitis, liver damage, pancreatitis, interstitial lung disease, and shingles reactivation can lead to dialysis, scarring, or organ failure. The list also includes multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children and newly onset type 1 diabetes.

Mandatory measures did not spare fertility and infant issues; cases of anti-sperm antibodies and autoimmune orchitis point to immune attacks that may impair male fertility. Cases of fetal distress, low birth weight, stillbirth, neonatal death, and neonatal vein thrombosis describe harms to the fetus and newborn.

This data was known, even as refusal was viewed as betrayal.

⭐️ Michael Saylor says Strategy and Strive can grow together 

🌐 Michael Saylor has argued that Strategy and Strive can compete for investor capital while helping each other expand the market for Bitcoin-backed preferred securities. Under Saylor’s terminology, Bitcoin represents “Digital Capital,” preferred securities such as Strategy’s STRC and Strive’s SATA represent “Digital Credit,” while MSTR and ASST sit in what he calls the “Digital Equity” category. The labels form part of Saylor’s own framework and are not formal regulatory asset classes.

📣 A 0.1% allocation from either pool would equal roughly $160 billion. Michael Saylor used that comparison to argue that Bitcoin treasury companies are competing mainly against much larger traditional equity and fixed-income markets, not only against one another. He wrote that Strategy and Strive may compete for the same individual investment, but a new investor learning how to assess one Bitcoin-linked preferred security could become more comfortable evaluating another. Saylor said several credible issuers could bring more research, trading liquidity and institutional attention to the category.

⚠️ The two companies remain separate businesses with different securities, liabilities and management decisions. Strategy issues STRC, while Strive issues SATA. Both are perpetual preferred securities, but their terms and dividend schedules differ. Strive said the purchase extended its SATA dividend reserve to 18 months, consisting at the time of 12 months of cash and another six months represented by STRC at prevailing market prices. The company described STRC as part of its reserve strategy, while stressing that market values can change.

⚡️ Iran will use all capabilities to counter any aggression: Foreign Ministry spokesperson

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iran is determined to use all its capabilities to repel any aggression against the country, Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei said, stressing that the country’s operational experience in “three rounds of heroic defense” had strengthened its readiness to confront threats.

In an exclusive interview with Tunisia’s Al-Chourouk newspaper, Baqaei addressed regional developments, Iran’s consultations with Oman on the Strait of Hormuz and prospects for regional security arrangements independent of foreign powers.
​
On maritime security, Baqaei said Iran and Oman, as the two coastal states bordering the strategic Strait of Hormuz, had a special responsibility to ensure safe navigation through the waterway.
​
He said Iran had consistently considered the security of maritime traffic in the area its responsibility over past decades. However, he noted that the waterway, as well as the territory and facilities of regional countries, had been used in recent months to plan and carry out military aggression against Iran, including attacks on residential areas and the killing of civilians.
​
Baqaei said such developments could not be overlooked in future arrangements for managing the strait.
​
He added that Tehran and Muscat had continued consultations in recent months to establish safe routes for commercial vessels and had reached an understanding on a temporary safe passage route, with some implementation details still under discussion.
​
He stressed that the bilateral understanding on a safe route should not be confused with the reopening or overall status of the Strait of Hormuz, noting that any sustainable, long-term mechanism for managing and securing the waterway must be developed with the participation and agreement of Iran and Oman, while taking their sovereignty and security concerns into account.
​
Third-party interference should not disrupt the process, he added.
​
Addressing the prospect of closer regional coordination against foreign military presence, Baqaei said recent developments had offered important lessons to neighboring countries and members of the Persian Gulf Cooperation Council.
​
He reiterated Iran’s position that regional security should be ensured by regional states themselves, stressing that the presence of foreign military powers had been a major source of insecurity.
​
Baqaei said Iran respected the national sovereignty, territorial integrity and security of regional countries and had no hostility toward its neighbors. He described good-neighborly relations, broader regional cooperation and the establishment of an indigenous security framework as longstanding principles of Iran’s foreign policy.
​
He said recent developments had created an opportunity for Persian Gulf countries to discuss the future of regional security from a more realistic perspective, without interference by powers from outside the region. Although such an arrangement would not emerge overnight, he added, continued dialogue and progress toward regional agreements were necessary steps.
​
Regarding the possibility of renewed confrontation with the US-Israeli alliance, Baqaei said Iran had consistently demonstrated its determination and capability to defend its sovereignty and territorial integrity against aggression and threats.
​
He reaffirmed Tehran’s resolve to mobilize all available capabilities to counter hostile actions, citing the country’s experience in three rounds of heroic defense against foreign aggression as an additional source of operational preparedness.

Crypto Idea

Something happened in the U.S. Treasury market that’s hard to ignore.

The quarter closed with 20-year Treasury yields at 5.68% and 30-year yields at 5.64%. These are levels the market hasn’t seen in more than 20 years. And this is no longer just a random spike lasting a couple of days, but a very noticeable shift in the cost of long-term borrowing.

Why are yields rising? Investors want an increasingly larger premium for lending money to the U.S. government for decades. The reasons are clear. Massive government debt, a large budget deficit, inflation that remains elevated, and a huge amount of new borrowing. In other words, the market is demanding an increasingly higher price for long-term U.S. debt.

And here’s the key question. What happens if 5% or 6% turn out not to be the ceiling, and yields eventually climb to 8%, 9%, or even 10%? For now, that’s not the base-case scenario, but if it happens, the rules of the game in financial markets will change dramatically.

Because when U.S. government bond yields hit 8%, investors face a simple question. Why take on significant risk in stocks, crypto, real estate, or gold when you can earn that kind of return in dollars from one of the most reliable financial instruments in the world? At that point, some capital could start flowing into Treasuries, and all other asset classes would have to offer significantly higher potential returns to remain attractive.

My takeaway is simple. Right now, it’s important to watch not just stocks and crypto, but the bond market as well. If the era of cheap money really is over, long-term Treasuries could become one of the key indicators of where global capital is headed next.
